questions.q: What is the primary goal of short-term containment?
options: Write the post-incident lessons-learned report
Permanently rebuild every affected system before taking any other action
Stop active damage right now, even if the fix is narrow or temporary
Classify the incident's severity level
questions.explain: Short-term containment runs on a fast clock: isolate, disable, or block immediately to stop the damage in front of you.

questions.q: Which of these is an example of long-term containment, as distinct from short-term containment?
options: Blocking a malicious IP address at the firewall
Isolating a host from the network the moment compromise is confirmed
Disabling a single compromised account
Rebuilding an affected system from a known-clean image while preserving the original for forensics
questions.explain: Rebuilding from a clean image (while preserving the original compromised system) is the durable, slower-clock response long-term containment covers.

questions.q: Why can leaving a short-term containment action in place indefinitely become a real risk?
options: Short-term containment actions automatically expire and reconnect attackers after 24 hours
It immediately triggers a second, unrelated incident
The isolated/disabled asset is still compromised underneath — it's quarantined, not cleaned, and can become a forgotten blind spot
It has no risk at all as long as the host stays isolated forever
questions.explain: An isolated host is still compromised; without the long-term rebuild/cleanup, it's a permanent blind spot rather than a resolved problem.

questions.q: In the compromised web server example, what was the short-term action and what was the long-term action?
options: Short-term: delete the server immediately. Long-term: notify customers
Short-term: isolate the server via EDR. Long-term: provision and verify a clean replacement, then forensically image the original
Short-term and long-term containment are the same single action in this example
Short-term: rebuild the server from a clean image. Long-term: isolate it from the network
questions.explain: Isolation is the fast, narrow move; provisioning a verified-clean replacement and preserving the original for forensics is the durable follow-through.

questions.q: Why does long-term containment typically involve preserving the original compromised system instead of wiping it right away?
options: So forensic analysis of what happened isn't lost once the replacement or cleanup is in place
Because short-term containment cannot legally be reversed
Preservation has no real purpose once a replacement system is live
Because wiping a system is always illegal
questions.explain: Preserving the original system or its image keeps forensic evidence available even after the business has moved on with a clean replacement.
